The index bijection j = p k holds for 1 ≤ k ≤ floor(N/p). The exact splitting H_N = p^(-s) H_floor(N/p) + U_N,p is unconditional for p > 0; primality and N < p^2 are not hypotheses of that equality.

N < p^2 implies floor(N/p) < p, making the actual prefix denominator prime to p. The explicit hypothesis that p does not divide its reduced numerator is retained. Positivity of the actual prefix supplies nonzero rational terms before padicValRat identities are applied.

The scaled-prefix term has valuation -s, whereas a nonzero remainder has nonnegative valuation. The proof treats the zero remainder separately and uses positivity of the full harmonic sum to satisfy the nonzero side conditions in the ultrametric equality.
Reducedness excludes a simultaneous p-factor in numerator and denominator. The negative rational valuation -s, with s > 0, therefore forces padicValNat p den(H_N) = s.

E_s,K is the product of actual positive prefix numerator magnitudes for 1 ≤ k ≤ K, so E_s,K > 0, even for K = 0 where the empty product is one. If 1 ≤ floor(N/p) ≤ K and p > E_s,K, then p cannot divide the relevant prefix numerator. K < p also implies N < p^2 from the floor bound.

Every admitted prime contributes p^s to den(H_N). Distinct primes give pairwise coprime prime powers, so their whole product divides the reduced denominator. The empty prime set yields the valid divisor one.

The positive product divisor is at most the positive reduced denominator. Monotonicity of log and the exact finite product-log identity give s Σ log p ≤ log den(H_N), without a prime-distribution hypothesis.

definition_candidate.definition_title: Harmonic nonmultiple remainder and explicit finite numerator exception product
definition_candidate.definition:
import Definitions.Def_ZetaNine_HarmonicStability

set_option autoImplicit false
open scoped BigOperators

namespace ZetaNine.HarmonicStability

/-- The sum of the actual harmonic terms whose index is not divisible by p. -/
def primeRemainder (s N p : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  ∑ j ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (fun j => ¬ p ∣ j), 1 / (j : ℚ) ^ s

/-- Product of the absolute reduced numerators of the actual first K harmonic prefixes. -/
def harmonicExceptionalProduct (s K : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∏ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, (harmonicPower s k).num.natAbs

end ZetaNine.HarmonicStability
definition_candidate.natural_language_statement:
For natural $s,N,p$, let $H_N^{(s)}=\sum_{j=1}^{N}j^{-s}$ be the rational generalized harmonic sum. Define

$$U_{s,N,p}=\sum_{\substack{1\le j\le N\\p\nmid j}}j^{-s},\qquad E_{s,K}=\prod_{k=1}^{K}\left|\operatorname{num}(H_k^{(s)})\right|.$$

The numerator is the reduced rational numerator and the product is one when $K=0$. Both objects are defined for all natural parameters. The module adds only these two finite expressions to the existing harmonic definition module; it contains no primality, unit, valuation, limit or PNT assertion.

theorem_candidates.theorem_title: Finite admitted prime powers divide the actual harmonic denominator
theorem_candidates.formal_statement:
theorem ZetaNine.HarmonicStability.harmonic_finite_prime_product_dvd (s K N : ℕ) (S : Finset ℕ)
    (hs : 0 < s)
    (hS : ∀ p ∈ S, p.Prime ∧ p ≤ N ∧ N / p ≤ K ∧ K < p ∧
      harmonicExceptionalProduct s K < p) :
    (∏ p ∈ S, p ^ s) ∣ (harmonicPower s N).den := by sorry
theorem_candidates.natural_language_statement:
Let $s>0$, $K,N\ge0$, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes. Put $H_N^{(s)}=\sum_{j=1}^{N}j^{-s}$ and

$$E_{s,K}=\prod_{k=1}^{K}\left|\operatorname{num}(H_k^{(s)})\right|.$$

Suppose every $p\in S$ satisfies

$$p\le N,\qquad \lfloor N/p\rfloor\le K,\qquad K<p,\qquad E_{s,K}<p.$$

Then the full finite prime-power product divides the reduced positive harmonic denominator:

$$\prod_{p\in S}p^s\mid\operatorname{den}(H_N^{(s)}).$$

All hypotheses refer to the actual finite harmonic prefixes. The explicit exception bound is a sufficient way to exclude their numerator prime factors; it is not a claim that every large prime is automatically a unit. The theorem supplies finite arithmetic and does not assert any asymptotic prime count or denominator growth rate.
theorem_candidates.explanation: Each admitted prime has $1\le\lfloor N/p\rfloor\le K<p$, hence $N<p^2$. Every possible reduced prefix numerator divides the positive integer $E_{s,K}$. Since $p>E_{s,K}$, that numerator is prime to $p$. Splitting the actual sum into its multiples of $p$ and its nonmultiple remainder gives $v_p(H_N^{(s)})=-s$, so its reduced denominator contains exactly $p^s$. Prime powers associated with distinct members of the finite set are coprime; multiplying these divisors proves the full product divisibility.

theorem_candidates.theorem_title: Finite prime logarithms bound the actual harmonic log denominator below
theorem_candidates.formal_statement:
theorem ZetaNine.HarmonicStability.harmonic_finite_prime_log_lower_bound (s K N : ℕ) (S : Finset ℕ)
    (hs : 0 < s)
    (hS : ∀ p ∈ S, p.Prime ∧ p ≤ N ∧ N / p ≤ K ∧ K < p ∧
      harmonicExceptionalProduct s K < p) :
    (s : ℝ) * (∑ p ∈ S, Real.log (p : ℝ)) ≤ logDen (harmonicPower s N) := by sorry
theorem_candidates.natural_language_statement:
Let $s>0$, $K,N\ge0$, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes. With $H_N^{(s)}=\sum_{j=1}^{N}j^{-s}$ and $E_{s,K}=\prod_{k=1}^{K}|\operatorname{num}(H_k^{(s)})|$, suppose every $p\in S$ satisfies

$$p\le N,\qquad \lfloor N/p\rfloor\le K,\qquad K<p,\qquad E_{s,K}<p.$$

Then

$$s\sum_{p\in S}\log p\le\log\operatorname{den}(H_N^{(s)}).$$

Here the denominator is fully reduced and positive. The finite inequality holds for every admitted finite prime set, including the empty set. It is the arithmetic lower bound before applying the prime number theorem; no asymptotic prime-distribution or full-sequence denominator-rate statement is part of the conclusion.
theorem_candidates.explanation: The finite-prime product theorem gives the positive divisor $\prod_{p\in S}p^s$ of the actual reduced denominator. Therefore that product is at most the denominator. Take natural logarithms and use the finite identity $\log\prod_{p\in S}p^s=s\sum_{p\in S}\log p$. The positivity needed for logarithmic monotonicity follows from primality and the positive reduced rational denominator.

theorem_candidates.theorem_title: A unit harmonic prefix forces the exact large-prime denominator exponent
theorem_candidates.formal_statement:
theorem ZetaNine.HarmonicStability.harmonic_large_prime_den_valuation (s N p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
    (hs : 0 < s) (hNp : p ≤ N) (hN : N < p ^ 2)
    (hunit : ¬ p ∣ (harmonicPower s (N / p)).num.natAbs) :
    padicValNat p (harmonicPower s N).den = s := by sorry
theorem_candidates.natural_language_statement:
Let $s>0$ and $N\ge0$, and let $p$ be prime with $p\le N<p^2$. If $p$ does not divide the reduced numerator of the actual prefix $H_{\lfloor N/p\rfloor}^{(s)}$, then

$$v_p\!\left(\operatorname{den}(H_N^{(s)})\right)=s,\qquad H_N^{(s)}=\sum_{j=1}^{N}j^{-s}.$$

The numerator-unit condition is essential. For example, $H_2^{(9)}=513/512$ has a factor $19$ in its numerator, and for $N=38,p=19$ the actual denominator exponent is eight instead of nine. The theorem concerns the exact reduced positive denominator for each admitted parameter; it does not invoke the prime number theorem.
theorem_candidates.explanation: Since $N<p^2$, the prefix length $\lfloor N/p\rfloor$ is below $p$, so its denominator is prime to $p$. The numerator hypothesis makes its rational $p$-adic valuation zero. In the exact splitting $H_N^{(s)}=p^{-s}H_{\lfloor N/p\rfloor}^{(s)}+U_{s,N,p}$, the first term has valuation $-s$, while the nonmultiple remainder is $p$-integral. Unequal valuations imply $v_p(H_N^{(s)})=-s$, with zero remainders handled separately. Reducedness then gives precisely exponent $s$ in the positive denominator.
